eips.title: Cap Deposit Requests Per Block
eips.summary: Proposed to cap deposit requests per block to enable 200M gas limit without breaking CLs; debated block building complexity and alternative approaches.

moments.context: Barnabas explained the concern: raising gas to 200M could exceed the 8192 deposit limit and break all CLs; discussed options including enforcing a limit on EL side.
Marius described the EIP's mechanism of counting deposits per transaction, discussed block building complexity, and floated the alternative of switching the deposit contract.
Nixo proposed PFI-ing 8254 to the Glamsterdam meta; Peter raised denial-of-service concerns about post-hoc invalidity; Barnabas confirmed he would PFI it.

After Marius noted CLs cannot handle more than 512 builder signatures, nixo asked whether 8254 could be proposed to Glamsterdam to address the last blocker to 200 million gas, with the details discussed async.

eips.summary: Proposed to remove the ETH burn feature of self-destruct for Glamsterdam; received broad support and was CFI'd.

Nixo confirmed support for CFI-ing 8246 in Glamsterdam after Peter supported removing just the burn as unlikely to cause real breakage.

eips.summary: Ignacio proposed for Hegota to resolve BLOCKHASH via the EIP-2935 system contract storage, repricing it to S-load cost for stateless execution witness consistency.

moments.context: Ignacio presented 7709 for Hegota: makes BLOCKHASH resolve via S-load against the 2935 system contract, eliminating a special case for stateless execution witnesses.
Felix questioned whether stateless clients would really lack the last 256 block hashes; Ignacio and Pavel argued the execution witness should be self-contained without external assumptions.

eips.title: Serve historical block hashes from state
eips.summary: Referenced as the system contract activated in Prague that stores block hash history, which 7709 would use for BLOCKHASH resolution.

moments.context: Ignacio explained that 7709 resolves BLOCKHASH via S-load against the EIP-2935 system contract storing 8000+ block hashes.

eips.title: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
eips.summary: Jochem presented proposal for Hegota to bump nonce of 28 remaining pre-Spurious-Dragon zero-nonce storage accounts, making EIP-7610 obsolete.

moments.context: Jochem presented EIP-8253: at the fork block, bump the nonce of 28 fossil accounts that have zero nonce, no code, but non-empty storage, removing the need for the 7610 collision check and simplifying the protocol.

eips.title: Revert creation in case of non-empty storage
eips.summary: Discussed as the EIP that 8253 would make obsolete by eliminating the pre-Spurious-Dragon accounts that necessitate its collision check.

moments.context: Jochem explained 7610 was PFI'd for Glamsterdam and handles contract collision checks for accounts with non-empty storage but zero nonce; 8253 would remove the need for it entirely.

eips.title: Revert creation in case of collision
eips.summary: Referenced as defining the contract collision check that only verifies nonce and code, not storage.

moments.context: Jochem explained EIP-684 defines how contract collision is checked — nonce and code only — which is why 7610 was needed for the zero-nonce storage edge case.

eips.title: State trie clearing (invariant-preserving alternative)
eips.summary: Referenced as the Spurious Dragon state-clearing EIP that bumped contract creation nonce to 1 and cleared empty accounts.

moments.context: Jochem cited EIP-161 as the change that bumped standard contract nonce to 1, noting 224 affected accounts existed at Spurious Dragon with 28 remaining today.
